chunks: Al-‘Iys ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
"When a man travels during the month of Ramadan, he breaks his fast."

And he said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله departed from al-Madinah to Makkah during the month of Ramadan, and the people were with him, including pedestrians. When he reached Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, he called for a cup of water between zuhr and ‘asr, then drank and broke his fast, and the people broke their fast with him. But some people persisted in their fasting, so he called them ‘the disobedient.’ Indeed, one only acts according to the command of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله."

key_terms.الْعُصَاةَ: the disobedient; those who opposed the Prophetic instruction
key_terms.بِأَمْرِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: by the command of the Messenger of Allah, indicating normative authority
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the prescribed time of fasting
key_terms.كُرَاعِ الْغَمِيمِ: Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, the place where this event occurred
key_terms.مُسَافِرًا: traveling; being on a journey that changes the fasting ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting while traveling in Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling that a traveler in the month of Ramadan breaks the fast. It also cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who broke his fast during travel and condemned those who insisted on continuing to fast, showing the authority of the Prophetic command in such legal matters.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1977 - Al-'Iys ibn Al-Qasim narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"When a man travels during the Month of Ramadan, he breaks his fast."

Imam (as) continued: "The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) departed from Medina to Mecca during Month of Ramadan, accompanied by people among whom were pedestrians. When he reached Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, between noon and afternoon, He called for a cup of water, drank, and broke his fast. The people with him also broke their fast, but some persisted in their fasting. He (sw) called them 'the disobedient,' as one is obligated to follow the command of the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family)."
